name_note: GTDB places this organism in the genus Schaedlerella and marks it as a split (_A) of the species described as Clostridium glycyrrhizinilyticum and later renamed Mediterraneibacter glycyrrhizinilyticus.

sentences.text: This organism was described as Clostridium glycyrrhizinilyticum after screening faecal bacteria for glycyrrhetic acid production by hydrolysis of glycyrrhizin yielded two isolated strains.
The strains were reported as Gram-positive, obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming rods belonging to cluster XIVa of the genus Clostridium.
Its 16S rRNA gene sequence showed roughly 94 to 95 per cent identity with validly described species including Ruminococcus gnavus and Ruminococcus torques.
A later study creating the genus Mediterraneibacter reclassified Clostridium glycyrrhizinilyticum as Mediterraneibacter glycyrrhizinilyticus, alongside several Ruminococcus species.
